ABSTRACT

Accurate and continuous monitoring of discharge in irrigation canals is essential for improving the transparency of water distribution in irrigation systems. This study presents a calibration approach based on the SonTek RS5 Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP) to adapt discharge estimates obtained from a Radar flow meter (RFM) into local hydraulic conditions. Field investigations were conducted at the PK 180 section of the “Left Branch” canal, which belongs to the South Mirzachul Canal (SMC) system. Using the ADCP, water level, canal width, wetted cross-sectional area, cross-sectionally averaged flow velocity, and discharge were measured, and these data were adopted as reference values for evaluating the RFM-based measurements. The water level and surface velocity recorded by the RFM were compared with the reference discharge determined using the ADCP. The comparisons showed that the standard computational algorithm of the radar device did not provide stable accuracy under all water-level conditions. Therefore, a velocity correction coefficient, K, which converts the RFM-measured surface velocity into the cross-sectionally averaged flow velocity, was evaluated, and its relationship with the relative canal width, B/h, was analyzed. The results showed that, within the study area, the K coefficient varied from 0.68 to 0.88, and its relationship with B/h demonstrated a high level of dependency (R² = 0.9511). After applying the correction coefficient, the RFM-based recalculated discharge values became closer to the ADCP reference values, while the relative errors remained within the range of −3.16% to +3.87%. The results indicate that the proposed approach can serve as an effective method for non-contact, continuous, and real-time discharge measurement and monitoring in lined irrigation networks.
